title: AI Data-Center Powered Land, Substation Headroom & BESS Site Optioning — Practitioner Testimony Operator Workbook
subtitle: Powered Land Qualification, Large-Load Interconnection Strategy, and Headroom Discovery Worksheets for AI Data-Center and BESS Site Optioning

worksheets.title: Powered Land Qualification and Hyperscale Load Economics
worksheets.purpose: Screen a candidate parcel against the rule that power is the site and acreage follows. This worksheet tests acreage, utility capacity, run-out costs, redundancy, site control, build economics and long-lead gear before any study fee or option payment leaves the account.
instructions: Start from available megawatts and work backward to land, fiber, water and gas; never begin with the parcel.
Call the utility before spending on studies, and log the department, the engineer and the exact capacity answer.
Write every cost in dollars with its source citation so the bid model can be audited line by line.
Model the downside case alongside the base case, including a lost tenant and a wrong power answer.
Leave no field blank; if a number is unknown, record the step and date by which it will be obtained.

fields.name: target_load_and_acreage
fields.prompt: State the target campus load in megawatts and the buildable acreage under control. Apply the 1MW per acre rule with a 100-acre floor, and explain whether the parcel clears the minimum that AI data center buyers require before they will look.
fields.example: Candidate parcel holds 140 buildable acres against a 120MW target, so it clears the floor with 20 acres of margin. Franklin Andrew Cruz sets the rule at 1MW per acre and warns that without a minimum of 100 acres buyers are not going to look [Franklin Andrew Cruz — YrpzmGX0-YM @ 00:00:47]. Status: qualified on acreage, pending power.

fields.name: utility_large_load_desk
fields.prompt: Record the utility contact and the exact question asked about supporting 100MW or more. Note which department handled the call, whether it serves 50MW-plus loads, and what capacity answer, line name, and timeline the engineers gave in return.
fields.example: Called the utility and asked directly whether it can support 100MW or more; the call was routed to the large-load department handling 50MW-plus requests, which is the desk that matters [Franklin Andrew Cruz — YrpzmGX0-YM @ 00:01:04]. Engineer named a 230 line as the candidate feed. Follow-up logged: request study scope, fee, and redundancy options in writing.

fields.name: study_fee_and_plan_b
fields.prompt: List the non-refundable utility study fees, rezoning budget, and upfront power security this site could demand. Then name the Plan B use, such as multifamily or a grocery-anchored commercial deal, that rescues the entitlement if the power answer comes back wrong.
fields.example: Study spend budgeted at the high end, since Advanta IRA warns you could spend 60 to 130, $140,000 just to hear the answer [Advanta IRA — 3rM3iGzRRUA @ 00:15:17]. Upfront power security reserved against the $22 million posted on one deal [Advanta IRA — 3rM3iGzRRUA @ 00:47:42]. Plan B: multifamily entitlement or a Kroger commercial deal [Advanta IRA — 3rM3iGzRRUA @ 00:17:30].

fields.name: powered_land_price_check
fields.prompt: Compare the asking price per acre against unpowered comparables and against powered-land comparables. State the multiple you are paying for power, and whether the premium is justified by a confirmed megawatt answer rather than a speculative hope of future capacity.
fields.example: Seller quotes a powered price near 4.5x the unpowered comparable, inside the 4x to 5x gap datacenterHawk reports in current deals [datacenterHawk — dTHn2ejpXvM @ 00:18:51]. Premium accepted only because the utility confirmed capacity in writing; without that letter, securing land without power is increasingly a speculative exercise [Environment+Energy Leader — wOKA9jWA8fw @ 00:08:10].

fields.name: power_and_fiber_run_out
fields.prompt: Measure the distance in miles from the parcel to the nearest usable transmission line and the nearest fiber route. Multiply each by the practitioner run-out cost per mile and record the total extension budget before any land price is agreed.
fields.example: Parcel sits 1.5 miles off the 230 line and 3 miles from the fiber route. At $20M per mile for power and $2M per mile for fiber, the run-out budget totals $30M plus $6M, or $36M [Advanta IRA — 3rM3iGzRRUA @ 00:08:27]. That figure now sits in the bid model as a direct deduction from the land offer.

fields.name: redundancy_source
fields.prompt: Name the redundancy source that backs the primary feed, such as a gas or coal plant, and describe how a second and third campus within roughly 50 kilometers could absorb spillover if one facility fails. Flag any territory lacking redundancy.
fields.example: Redundancy source identified as a gas plant on the same transmission corridor, because the cost of downtime is very high [LandApp by LandGate — 0_owMAznas0 @ 00:08:54]. Embry's Decatur, Alabama site died for lack of redundancy in TVA territory [Advanta IRA — 3rM3iGzRRUA @ 00:30:40]. Two sister parcels sit inside 50 kilometers for spillover [Southern Economic Development Council — yg9V2befNR0 @ 00:25:19].

fields.name: site_control_option
fields.prompt: Describe the site-control instrument, including option term, consideration paid, extension rights, and how each leg of any put and call is papered. Confirm the landowner compared multiple offers and that no developer can tie up the land for years without paying.
fields.example: Two-year paid option with annual extension fees; the landowner compared three offers side by side before signing [US Energy Weekly — JwCWz91cMQc @ 00:05:01]. Put and call legs carry separate certificates, because a 66ZF certificate on the call did not cover the put and let a buyer exit 13 contracts [Maclarens Lawyers — q09nIjF9s5c @ 00:04:50].

fields.name: build_cost_and_breakeven
fields.prompt: Estimate total build cost using a per-megawatt range, then add engineering fees and contingency. Record the expected rate per kilowatt per month and the utilization needed to break even, and model the one-tenant-exit case against that break-even floor.
fields.example: 20MW shell priced at $10M per MW, about $200M, before 15-20% engineering fees and a 15-25% contingency [Your Finance Uncle — BXuRdYxfF2k @ 00:03:08]. Break-even sits at 60-65% utilization at $150/kW/month plus 15% ancillary revenue [Your Finance Uncle — BXuRdYxfF2k @ 00:09:33]. Losing one tenant drops utilization to 50% and puts the site underwater [Your Finance Uncle — BXuRdYxfF2k @ 00:13:56].

fields.name: rack_density_and_pue
fields.prompt: Record the design rack density in kilowatts per rack and the target PUE. Convert the IT load into total facility draw, then price the annual electricity cost of any PUE gap against a competing site using a stated cost per kilowatt-hour.
fields.example: Design density set at 130 kW per rack, inside the 120-140 kW range for AI racks versus about 10 kW a decade ago [The Power Engineer — BWtk0CSPH6g @ 00:00:18]. On 100 MW of IT, PUE 1.5 draws 150 MW against 120 MW at PUE 1.2, a gap worth about $26M per year at $0.10/kWh [BESS Engineer — MnGAkKrZF_I @ 00:01:01].

fields.name: long_lead_gear
fields.prompt: List every long-lead electrical item, including large transformers and grid gear, with its quoted lead time and order status. Note whether the general contractor joined design for constructability review, and which prefabricated modular components will compress the schedule.
fields.example: Large transformers carry three-to-four-year lead times and grid gear two-plus years, so both purchase orders are placed now; you can't download another transformer [BUILT BENEATH — 7L7MfK9coTY @ 00:06:39]. The GC joined design for constructability and value engineering, with prefabricated modular electrical rooms tightening quality control [MEP Engineer AJ — lTK_pU1_uFc @ 00:05:15].

worksheets.completion_gate: Do not pay a study fee or sign an option until the parcel clears 100 acres, a named line and redundancy source are confirmed, a Plan B use is documented, and the one-tenant-exit case still covers costs.

worksheets.title: Large-Load Interconnection and Cluster Cost Exposure
worksheets.purpose: Map the interconnection path in PJM, ERCOT or a cluster-study region, and size the cash, evidence and equipment commitments each path demands. The worksheet forces a priced view of security, forecast discounting, ride-through, registration and withdrawal exposure.
instructions: Size every filing in the unit the operator counts, such as UCAP for PJM expedited requests, never nameplate.
Discount headline queue totals before using them, and record the adjusted figure next to the original.
Price security, deposits and the full withdrawal ladder in dollars before any money is posted.
Choose equipment on delivery timeline and record the order date for every high-voltage transformer and breaker.
Attach the citation for every threshold, deadline and penalty so the filing team can verify it.

fields.name: iso_path_and_threshold
fields.prompt: Identify the ISO or RTO, the requested load in megawatts, and whether it crosses the ERCOT 75 MW large-load threshold or the PJM 250 MW UCAP expedited threshold. Record the first path you will enter and the path you will migrate to.
fields.example: PJM campus enters as non-capacity-backed load accepting pre-emergency curtailment, then migrates to bring-your-own-generation, because strategy is about sequencing, not just selecting [Keentel Engineering — C9tZQM-x_Ho @ 00:05:42]. Expedited track filing sized at 300 MW UCAP, not nameplate, clearing the more-than-250 MW floor [Keentel Engineering — C9tZQM-x_Ho @ 00:02:58]. No site, fuel or MW changes are permitted after filing.

fields.name: entry_security_and_deposit
fields.prompt: Calculate the cash required to enter the queue: ERCOT Batch Zero security per megawatt or the PJM expedited non-refundable deposit per megawatt. State the total dollars, the posting deadline, and who on the team approves releasing that capital.
fields.example: A 200 MW ERCOT load posts $50,000/MW, or $10M, with the TDSP submission by July 10, alongside site control, duplicate-request disclosure and engineering documents [WhyPKD — EvpNriZrrME @ 00:02:47]. The rule exists so only truly capitalized projects can move forward and other rate payers are protected [WhyPKD — EvpNriZrrME @ 00:05:03]. CFO signs the release.

fields.name: forecast_discount_evidence
fields.prompt: Document the evidence that will keep your megawatts counted in the operator forecast: milestones, ramp data, utilization evidence, and duplication disclosure. Estimate the discount the operator applies to your online year and how your filings beat it.
fields.example: PJM applies forecast discounting based on when the project comes online, about 40% in middle years and about 33% later [Keentel Engineering — C9tZQM-x_Ho @ 00:04:05]. Filing package includes milestones, ramp data, utilization evidence and duplication disclosure, because a signed utility contract does not mean the MW are counted [Keentel Engineering — C9tZQM-x_Ho @ 00:04:21].

fields.name: queue_reality_haircut
fields.prompt: Record the date-stamped headline queue total for the zone, then apply a reality haircut using adjusted forecasts and duplicate-request evidence. State how many real megawatts likely stand ahead of yours and how that changes your energization assumption.
fields.example: ERCOT forecasters cut 218 GW of letters, contracts and third-party forecasts to 148 GW by about 2032 [Data Centers Technical Info — S8vmSHwFrvE @ 00:04:08]. Duplicate shopping inflates totals: one 400MW requirement shopped by four to five developers showed up as 2GW of requests [datacenterHawk — dTHn2ejpXvM @ 00:15:10]. Planning assumes roughly two-thirds of headline load is real.

fields.name: ride_through_settings
fields.prompt: Describe the backup generator and UPS control sequence during a voltage sag. Confirm generators start but delay transfer until the ride-through window expires, that loaded settings are verified, and that power quality is recorded at the point of service.
fields.example: Generators programmed to start on sag but hold transfer until the ride-through window expires; loaded settings verified and sags included in IST [Keentel Engineering — WN6PtJ3kQDQ @ 00:13:03]. The risk is real: ERCOT has seen over a dozen events in a year where hundreds of megawatts unexpectedly left the grid [Data Centers Technical Info — S8vmSHwFrvE @ 00:21:27].

fields.name: procurement_and_study_validity
fields.prompt: List the high-voltage transformers and breakers purchased, their quoted lead times, and site preparation started. Explain how these actions protect the study from invalidation, and pick each item on delivery timeline rather than technical optimality, with a short justification.
fields.example: High-voltage breakers ordered at 125 weeks, up from 77 weeks in 2023 [Profound Studies — dMPUECoTe2M @ 00:01:40]. Transformers purchased and site prep begun, since otherwise ERCOT invalidates the study, resets energization to 01/01/2028 and reallocates the megawatts [James Dickey — 9zpO8wwsfXc @ 02:34:36]. Vendor B chosen because it lands within a year [The Clean Energy Edge Podcast — kHFYcexB2dU @ 00:09:25].

fields.name: nerc_registration_check
fields.prompt: Add up every MVA of load and storage at the site, including any planned battery. State whether the total crosses the 20 MVA and 60 kV Category 2 registration threshold, and what compliance obligations follow before the battery is ordered.
fields.example: Existing site registers 18 MVA; the proposed battery adds 4 MVA for 22 MVA total, which crosses the 20 MVA and 60 kV Category 2 threshold [Keentel Engineering — f1C-d4m7OHg @ 00:03:20]. Registration recount triggers a compliance review before procurement. Option under study: trim battery inverter rating so the site stays below the threshold.

fields.name: cluster_cost_allocation
fields.prompt: Record the cluster or study your project sits in, the neighbors sharing upgrades, and the allocated network upgrade cost in dollars per kilowatt. Flag any estimate above $100/kW as a kill risk and note how far it moved between studies.
fields.example: Cluster allocation came back at $140/kW, above the $100/kW line that makes withdrawal 22 percentage points more likely; 13% of estimates move more than $100/kW between studies [Environmental Defense Fund — M62wgLYBKBw @ 00:33:36]. Costs are coupled to neighbors [Keentel Engineering — gGBYCEdn18o @ 00:04:44], and the real risk may sit many electrical miles from the POI [Keentel Engineering — TM7qt8CCWxk @ 00:07:20].

fields.name: withdrawal_ladder
fields.prompt: Price the withdrawal penalty ladder before posting any security. Using your allocated upgrade cost, calculate the exit cost at each penalty step, including the 20% step after the LGIA, and name the decision point at which you would withdraw.
fields.example: On 200 MW with $178M allocated, exits run $8.9M at 5%, $17.88M at 10% and $35.6M at 20% [Keentel Engineering — TM7qt8CCWxk @ 00:09:17]. Decision point set before the 20% step after the LGIA. For an arbitrage-focused BESS, the ERIS downgrade option is modeled to shed deliverability-driven upgrade exposure [Keentel Engineering — TM7qt8CCWxk @ 00:13:03].

fields.name: poi_screening_and_readiness
fields.prompt: Describe how candidate POIs were screened before filing, including DFAX runs, multiple project sizes, and model readiness. Confirm site control covers the gen-tie all the way to the POI and explain whether revenue is booked only after synchronization.
fields.example: Three POIs screened with DFAX at 150, 200 and 250 MW, PSSE and PSCAD models ready, and the study shadowed [Keentel Engineering — TM7qt8CCWxk @ 00:19:45]. Site control locked along the gen-tie to the POI [WIRES — -BTpIv2G5-0 @ 01:05:27]. No revenue booked at SGIA signing, since a failed model quality test slips sync a full quarterly cycle [Keentel Engineering — YabOCr0t9pI @ 00:00:58].

worksheets.completion_gate: Advance only when entry security is funded, the forecast evidence package is filed, long-lead gear is purchased, registration thresholds are recounted, and every upgrade estimate above $100/kW has a written re-price or withdrawal decision.

worksheets.title: Wholesale Market Read, Queue Wait Cost and Headroom Discovery
worksheets.purpose: Translate grid-operator rules, nodal prices and queue attrition into a dated cost of waiting, then locate real headroom on hosting capacity and POI heat maps. The worksheet pairs market revenue logic with substation and ground diligence for both load and BESS sites.
instructions: Quote every queue number and map value with its snapshot or refresh date.
Treat every published hosting capacity figure as a screening ceiling, not a connection right.
Convert upgrade estimates into dollars per kilowatt and compare them with completed and withdrawn benchmarks.
Stack BESS revenue streams explicitly and model curtailment for hours when the wires are full.
Check the parent substation, the binding constraint and ground conditions before freezing a candidate site.

fields.name: grid_operator_and_market
fields.prompt: Name the grid operator and market structure governing the site, whether an energy-only market or a capacity market. Explain how that structure pays for megawatts versus megawatt-hours and what it means for firm load and storage revenue.
fields.example: Site sits in PJM, whose capacity market secures enough power for consumers three years in the future [pjminterconnection — ulpPgF6UT1E @ 00:00:23], paying providers regardless of whether energy is produced [CME Group — dYvEG3uQzsQ @ 00:02:55]. Storage spec reads 10 MW rated power and 20 MWh stored energy, keeping the two units separate [Modo Energy — OIAK1RATT9M @ 00:02:06].

fields.name: nodal_price_read
fields.prompt: Record the nodal LMP pattern at the candidate node, including typical spreads, System Lambda relationship, and scarcity adders. Explain what the spread says about transmission need and whether the node favors load siting, storage arbitrage, or both.
fields.example: Candidate ERCOT node prices well below congested city nodes, matching the pattern of cheap power near West Texas wind farms; the spread maps where the grid needs transmission [US Energy Weekly — sxulqIJRZrM @ 00:03:18]. ORDC adders and the $5,000/MWh cap set the upside in this energy-only market, so arbitrage value is modeled at the node.

fields.name: queue_snapshot_and_wait
fields.prompt: Record the date-stamped queue snapshot for the region, the number of projects and gigawatts ahead, and the median request-to-operation wait. Translate that wait into an expected commercial operation date and note how solid the projects ahead appear.
fields.example: ERCOT GIS Report snapshot shows nearly 2,000 projects totaling 432 GW, more than five times Texas peak demand [US Energy Weekly — DzkVggOvJGs @ 00:00:01]; the date is logged because the report is monthly [US Energy Weekly — DzkVggOvJGs @ 00:04:20]. Median wait for 2025 builds ran 61 months [THE PHYSICAL LAYER — v5uOMJOzPbk @ 00:04:02], so COD assumes five years.

fields.name: attrition_and_completion
fields.prompt: Estimate the attrition rate among projects ahead of yours using historical completion and withdrawal data. State what share of the headline queue is likely to be built and how that attrition could shift upgrade costs onto your remaining project.
fields.example: Only about 13% of 2000-2020 requested capacity was online by end-2025 and 75% withdrew, with withdrawals above 40% even after a signed agreement [The Pharos Project — Br7K7fGD4uk @ 00:01:29]. Attrition is priced into the timeline because only a fraction of the headline queue will ever get built [US Energy Weekly — DzkVggOvJGs @ 00:04:41].

fields.name: upgrade_cost_per_kw
fields.prompt: Divide the network upgrade estimate by project kilowatts and record the dollars per kilowatt. Compare that figure with what completed projects paid and what withdrawn projects faced, and state whether the result signals proceed, re-price, or kill.
fields.example: Upgrade estimate of $12M on a 100 MW project equals $120/kW, well above the roughly $84/kW completed projects paid and below the roughly $600 that quitters faced [Wattlore — CDd-hsI3tKQ @ 00:04:31]. Benchmark warning: one 51 MW solar farm drew a $598 million bill, more than $11,000 per kW [Wattlore — CDd-hsI3tKQ @ 00:04:14]. Verdict: re-price.

fields.name: bess_revenue_stack
fields.prompt: List each BESS revenue stream available at the node, such as arbitrage, balancing, and capacity, and the route-to-market provider that will trade the asset. Note curtailment exposure on connect-and-manage sites when the wires are full, and its revenue impact.
fields.example: Revenue stack combines arbitrage, balancing and capacity, since a single stream rarely justifies the investment; one route-to-market provider trades the asset, carries imbalance and sells balancing services [learnBESS — m0yVO4ZOmdc @ 00:02:01]. Connect-and-manage curtailment modeled for hours when the wires are full, because it hits revenue directly [US Energy Weekly — DzkVggOvJGs @ 00:04:55].

fields.name: hosting_capacity_map_read
fields.prompt: Record the hosting capacity value shown on the utility map for the candidate feeder or substation, the layer setting used, and the refresh date. Explain why the figure is treated as a screening ceiling and not a connection right.
fields.example: National Grid shows 6.65 MW available on Foxboro 2, with 350 kW connected and an 8 MVA bank at 75% loaded [National Grid Distributed Generation — KxAPuQUu_II @ 00:10:39]. Layer switched to connected plus pending. Value logged as a ceiling, since a recloser without voltage supervisory control drags downstream values lower [National Grid Distributed Generation — KxAPuQUu_II @ 00:14:37].

fields.name: substation_proximity_and_parent
fields.prompt: Record the distance from the site to the nearest substation and the available capacity at its parent high-voltage substation. Note any voltage step-downs downstream that reduce hosting capacity, and any swamps or topography issues visible near the feeder.
fields.example: Nearest LV substation measured at 240 meters, inside ESB's 300-meter rule; parent HV substation clicked and its available capacity checked [ESB Networks — fqIsW9Rhp48 @ 00:03:29]. Topography basemap flagged a swamp beside the candidate feeder, and a 13.8 kV to 4 kV step-down lowers downstream hosting capacity [National Grid Distributed Generation — KxAPuQUu_II @ 00:12:49].

fields.name: binding_constraint_and_profile
fields.prompt: Identify the binding hosting constraint from the power-flow study, whether line loading or connection-point voltage. Record the storage operating profile handed to the utility and whether the feeder penetration level triggers supplementary studies under local rules.
fields.example: PowerFactory run shows the maximum voltage limit at the connection point is the limiting factor [DIgSILENT GmbH – Power System Solutions — 7iequWeuZTQ @ 00:04:28]. Peak-shaving operating profile delivered so the utility avoids studying the conservative frequency-regulation case [Energy Storage Assocation — Mk3XaANjMd4 @ 00:47:25]. Feeder penetration sits above 15%, so supplementary studies apply [LUMA — UnmedCjwEb0 @ 00:04:49].

fields.name: ground_and_heatmap_diligence
fields.prompt: Summarize ground diligence on geology, karst, sinkholes, water tables, and baseline deformation, plus the date of the most recent POI heat map refresh. Price the cost of a one-month delay for the planned facility size and name who signs off.
fields.example: Geology, karst, sinkhole, water-table and ground-deformation screens completed before earthworks, since one month of delay on a 60 MW facility can cost up to $14 million [KorrAI — MvUw50RZNRQ @ 00:00:55]. CAISO POI heat map pulled on its post-cluster refresh, which lands 30 calendar days after each cluster study [California ISO — YAtPW03BCrY @ 00:00:19].

worksheets.completion_gate: Shortlist a site only when its queue position is dated, upgrade cost per kilowatt is benchmarked, a stacked revenue case survives curtailment, parent substation capacity is confirmed, and ground diligence is complete before earthworks.

worksheets.title: Substation, Transformer and Behind-the-Meter Power Plan
worksheets.purpose: Lock the power chain from the transmission bus to the rack before money moves. This worksheet puts the large power transformer, substation topology, ERCOT model package and on-site gas plant into one register so that lead times, redundancy, air permits and the battery buffer are settled before equipment lands on site.
instructions: Start with the transformer register, because the large power transformer is the gating item, with quoted lead times running from 122 weeks to 3 to 4 years.
Record every lead time with the vendor name and the date of the quote, and keep grid queue position on a separate line from equipment delivery.
Treat a radial single-source feed as a defect to be designed out unless a named redundancy path is documented and owned.
For behind-the-meter plants, never size the fleet to the load; show the overbuild, the spare units and the battery layer explicitly.
Leave no field blank; write 'unknown' with an owner and a due date wherever an answer is still pending.

fields.name: transformer_lead_time_register
fields.prompt: List every large power transformer and high-voltage breaker the site needs, the lead time each vendor quoted, and the date the quote was received. State whether the order is placed now or waiting on design, and name the gating item.
fields.example: Main power transformer quoted at 122 weeks by APG CEO Dan Girard after first misspeaking it as 60 months [REsource Labs — lFIWqD0EAkM @ 00:09:23]. Breakers carried at roughly 40 weeks on the same fast-track path. The transformer is the gating item, so the order is released at the 60% design stage rather than at IFC [Keentel Engineering — GAM0L1fXtiA @ 00:09:23].

fields.name: approved_manufacturer_check
fields.prompt: Record whether the transmission operator's approved-manufacturer list has been obtained before any transformer quote or order. Name the operator, the date the list was pulled, and any vendor or country of origin that falls outside the approved set.
fields.example: Approved-manufacturer list requested from the transmission operator before any quoting began, because some Chinese units are not approved [Ryne Ogren — 6_osryMHPf4 @ 00:04:19]. Two quotes from unlisted factories were struck from the bid tab. Queue position is tracked on a separate line, since a transformer delivered early cannot fix missing grid capacity [Critical Systems Explained — uEz7S-WjHG0 @ 00:07:29].

fields.name: substation_topology
fields.prompt: Describe the planned substation layout as radial, tapped, LILO, interconnected or 2N redundant, and explain how the chosen path removes single-source failure. State whether the substation is owned, the design voltage standard, and the products used to build it.
fields.example: Owned substation with an interconnected, 2N path instead of a radial single-source feed, which eliminates the path failure point [Base Config — giNYYY0DnJw @ 00:02:09]. Designed to the 345 kV standard but built with 230 kV products to speed delivery [REsource Labs — lFIWqD0EAkM @ 00:12:41]. Bays are laid out once in the model so they are only made one time.

fields.name: design_milestone_gates
fields.prompt: Log the dates for the 30%, 60%, 90% and issued-for-construction substation design milestones. Identify which unresolved items sit in the risk window between 30% and 60%, and which items are flagged as unspecified before the 30% handoff.
fields.example: Design is gated at 30-60-90-IFC, with the risk window held between 30% and 60% [Keentel Engineering — GAM0L1fXtiA @ 00:09:23]. Before the 30% handoff, BOM balloons flag unspecified items in red and catch stray objects parked at the origin [primtech solutions — 2FBThdUqgRg @ 00:43:02]. Three red balloons remain on grounding and PT fusing.

fields.name: ercot_sb6_model_package
fields.prompt: For any load above 75 MW in ERCOT, list the PSCAD and positive-sequence models, ride-through curves, harmonic data and fault contributions already delivered. Record the post-trip short-circuit ratio at the bus and whether early EMT screening has run.
fields.example: Campus sits above the 75 MW SB6 threshold, so PSCAD and positive-sequence models, ride-through curves, harmonic data and fault contributions go in before ordering [Keentel Engineering — u_aIABsRd0A @ 00:02:11]. On a 1,000 MW campus at a 345 kV bus, one line trip leaves a short-circuit ratio near 3.9, close to the instability floor of 3 [Keentel Engineering — u_aIABsRd0A @ 00:03:52].

fields.name: energization_checklist
fields.prompt: Record the pre-energization checks for the substation, including grounding straps on the neutral grounding reactor and fuse ratings on every potential transformer. Name the person who signed each check and the date, and note any curtailment exposure if energization slips.
fields.example: Factory ground strap removed from the neutral grounding reactor, because it bypasses the reactor, and every PT confirmed with a 5 A fuse [SpeedFreakLS1 — -RBp8jOUA1U @ 00:19:13]. Signed by the commissioning lead before closing in. Curtailment risk is logged because a 150 MW farm can be cut to 20 or 50 MW within minutes [SpeedFreakLS1 — -RBp8jOUA1U @ 00:02:45].

fields.name: btm_fleet_sizing
fields.prompt: State the firm megawatt target for the behind-the-meter plant, the unit size and count installed, and the spare units carried for reliability. Show the reliability target, explain why the fleet is not sized to the load, and confirm N plus two coverage.
fields.example: 250 MW firm islanded campus served by 115 recip units of 2.5 MW, or 290 MW installed, reaching three nines where 100 base units give zero statistical reliability [Collicutt Energy Services — CVfxSDNW3G4 @ 00:26:50]. Fleet is sized N plus two so one unit can be down for its oil change without missing target [Uintah County Economic Development (Official) — 169FuRa1T-0 @ 00:14:19].

fields.name: air_permit_path
fields.prompt: Name the air district, its attainment status, and whether the plant stays under the minor new source review 250 tons per year threshold. Identify the air consultant, the emission controls proposed, and the plan for emission reduction credit trading and banking.
fields.example: Site location checked first, then the plant confirmed under the minor new source review 250 tons per year threshold [VoltaGrid — rQu_8zcOaZU @ 00:02:59]. Selective catalytic reduction cutting NOx 98 percent is the model, after 200 MW was permitted in 21 days in a severe nonattainment zone [VoltaGrid — rQu_8zcOaZU @ 00:02:16]. Air consultant named; credit banking plan attached.

fields.name: load_buffer_and_protection
fields.prompt: Describe the battery layer placed between the generators and the AI training or inference load, its megawatt and duration sizing, and the status of compensation, protection and control design for island mode before generation equipment arrives on site.
fields.example: Generators never couple directly to AI load; a battery layer protects the power plant from load swings [Collicutt Energy Services — CVfxSDNW3G4 @ 00:36:22]. Starting size is about 30 percent of designed gas capacity at two-hour duration [Uintah County Economic Development (Official) — 169FuRa1T-0 @ 00:18:34]. Island-mode protection and control closed out before equipment lands [The Machine Room Podcast — rED467a2820 @ 00:16:43].

fields.name: fuel_bridge_and_exit
fields.prompt: Explain how fuel reaches the plant before the pipeline is built, who owns the compressors, trucks and trailers, and what happens to the generation fleet when the grid arrives. State whether the plant is a bridge or a permanent asset, and price any stranding.
fields.example: Pipeline gas compressed into CNG and trucked as a virtual pipeline, with the developer owning compressors, trucks and trailers [VoltaGrid — rQu_8zcOaZU @ 00:01:10]. Exit planned on day one: recip units jacked and rolled out or run as a peaker, and the freed hall converted to data-center space [Collicutt Energy Services — CVfxSDNW3G4 @ 00:48:27]. Lower utilization is priced as stranded power.

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 4 is complete only when the transformer order date and approved-manufacturer check are recorded, the substation path removes single-source failure, ERCOT SB6 models are delivered for loads above 75 MW, the behind-the-meter fleet is sized N plus two with a battery buffer, and island-mode protection and control is closed out before equipment lands.

worksheets.title: BESS Design, Sizing and Revenue Stack
worksheets.purpose: Turn the battery from a box of cells into a bankable power plant. This worksheet fixes the power-versus-energy answer, the AC block and skid budget, the EMS setup, commissioning safeguards, grid distance, land, revenue stack and warranty terms before any supply contract is signed.
instructions: Answer power or capacity first; chemistry, container format and cost basis all follow from that single answer.
Fix one revenue application before procurement, because EMS, PCS and thermal design differ between frequency-response and arbitrage builds.
Measure grid distance in kilometers to the point of connection, using about 1 km as the target radius and treating anything beyond 5 km as dead.
Price EMS fees, SCADA and real round-trip efficiency inside the contract, with the technical specification attached as an annex.
Assume integration, assembly and construction will cause most faults, and name an accountable party for each commissioning safeguard.

fields.name: power_vs_energy_requirement
fields.prompt: State whether the site needs power or capacity first, giving the megawatt swing to buffer and the megawatt-hours to store. Explain which chemistry and container format matches that answer and how the footprint changes between the options considered.
fields.example: Power comes first: a 100 MW site sees GPU swings of 40 to 50 MW [Energy Institute, University of Texas at Austin — HhLc8bnBSIo @ 00:09:21]. A 20-ft LTO box pushes 3 MW, while an LFP box of the same footprint holds nearly 10 times the energy but delivers only 2 MW [Energy Institute, University of Texas at Austin — HhLc8bnBSIo @ 00:10:54].

fields.name: cost_basis_comparison
fields.prompt: Compare the shortlisted systems on cost per kilowatt and cost per kilowatt-hour, and state which basis matters for this application. Note the chemistry, the vendor quote date, and whether the procurement route is turnkey or split across separate PCS and battery vendors.
fields.example: Energy-priced LFP benchmark at about $550 per kW and roughly $270 per kWh, against power-priced LTO near $3,500 per kWh but $600 per kW [Energy Institute, University of Texas at Austin — HhLc8bnBSIo @ 00:23:14]. Split procurement, with PCS and battery from different vendors, chosen after turnkey pricing came in higher [Inel Institute of Technology — 5K3HSEyhIng @ 01:02:58].

fields.name: ac_block_architecture
fields.prompt: Lay out the AC block: containers per PCS-transformer skid, energy per container, C-rate, and cooling method. Break down the medium-voltage skid budget by PCS, transformer, switchgear and structure, and flag where an isolation transformer is required for unstable grid supply.
fields.example: Four 5 MWh containers per PCS-transformer skid at 0.5C, a 2-hour charge-discharge rate [Cummins — RRbdgfTqeTA @ 00:03:16]. Skid budget: PCS 40-50%, transformer 20-30%, switchgear 10-15%, structure 10-20% [BESS Engineer — H7C34V05QQw @ 00:02:27]. Isolation transformer placed behind the PCS because site grid electricity is not stable [ELFBULB Battery — NZa3fz23P5Q @ 00:02:15].

fields.name: ems_configuration
fields.prompt: Describe how the EMS is configured to the real site, including tariff swings, load-shedding pattern and the single revenue application fixed before procurement. Note whether solar and BESS share an inverter and the reliability tradeoff that choice creates.
fields.example: EMS set to the measured tariff swings and load-shedding pattern, not to the application the user describes [Gaurav J - TheElectricalGuy — Bg-6ClEVMSU @ 00:10:13]. Arbitrage is fixed as the single application before procurement [Gaurav J - TheElectricalGuy — Bg-6ClEVMSU @ 00:13:38]. Separate solar and BESS inverters keep one source available during maintenance [Inel Institute of Technology — 5K3HSEyhIng @ 01:10:40].

fields.name: commissioning_safety_limits
fields.prompt: List the commissioning safeguards: monitoring and communication systems online before racks energize, insulation-loss alarms routed to a live operator with escalation, and locked limits on state of charge, voltage, current and temperature. Name the integration contractor accountable.
fields.example: Monitoring confirmed online before energizing, after Victoria Big Battery's coolant leak cascaded across two units [Power System Operation Slides — 7tln9f5Ak7M @ 00:08:25]. Insulation-loss alarms escalate to a live operator, since unescalated alarms preceded fire at Moss Landing by two days [Power System Operation Slides — 7tln9f5Ak7M @ 00:07:48]. Integration drives 65% of faults [Power System Operation Slides — Xys0DmLCtVk @ 00:02:08].

fields.name: grid_distance_screen
fields.prompt: Measure the distance from the candidate BESS parcel to the point of connection, the cable cost per kilometer, and whether network-upgrade allocations threaten the project. Record the decision to proceed, re-price or kill before paying for mid-stage engineering.
fields.example: Parcel sits 0.8 km from the point of connection, inside the roughly 1 km radius Harmony uses, where cabling can run up to £10m per km [Regen — Zmu3gs7y51A @ 00:34:31]. Upgrade allocation screened before mid-stage engineering, because tens to hundreds of millions of dollars can kill a project [Modo Energy — LhT4VVDW7CI @ 00:14:10]. Decision: proceed.

fields.name: land_footprint_and_lease
fields.prompt: Record the acreage needed for the planned megawatt-hours, the energy density assumed per acre, extra acres held for noise setback, and the lease or purchase terms. Include rent per acre and any revenue-share percentage offered to the landowner.
fields.example: Density set at 50 MWh per acre, the lower side of a 100 MWh ceiling [The Land Department Podcast — bWbMkkvRPWI @ 00:08:20]. Ten to 20 extra acres bought for noise setback, avoiding a roughly $2 million sound wall [The Land Department Podcast — bWbMkkvRPWI @ 00:17:16]. Rent benchmark: £10,000 to £40,000 per acre per year [Solar Grid Check — 9mZg--94z1I @ 00:00:00].

fields.name: revenue_stack
fields.prompt: Break the expected revenue into arbitrage, ancillary or frequency-response services and capacity, with the share each stream contributes. Name the route-to-market or EMS provider, its fee as a share of arbitrage revenue, and SCADA costs written into the contract.
fields.example: Stack modeled on arbitrage, ancillary services and capacity, with location setting the spread, since location is everything for how batteries make money [Modo Energy — AtMNJWhrmXE @ 00:01:46]. EMS fees can take 20 to 30 percent of arbitrage, and SCADA can cost as much as a container [Jerzy Kuzminski — fDBjJyTGWDQ @ 00:22:19]. Both are priced before signing.

fields.name: node_selection_and_timeline
fields.prompt: Identify the target node, how many other developers are pursuing it, and the second- and third-best alternatives evaluated. State the expected interconnection timeline for the market and any capacity growth secured inside the same footprint during development.
fields.example: Three other developers target the best node, so the second- and third-best nodes are under evaluation [Clearspot — tFP2z1s7IrM @ 00:06:15]. ERCOT interconnection runs around 3 years against up to 7 in CAISO. Footprint reserved for growth, following a project that rose from 200 MW in September 2023 to 300 MW six months later [Regen — Zmu3gs7y51A @ 00:25:44].

fields.name: warranty_and_supply_contract
fields.prompt: Record the warranty state-of-charge window and cycle assumptions, how dispatch stays inside them, and whether the technical specification is a contract annex. Note when insurers were brought in and how battery and transformer suppliers were vetted for bankability.
fields.example: Dispatch held between 5% and 95% state of charge and below warranty cycle assumptions [Clearspot — tFP2z1s7IrM @ 00:32:43]. Technical specification attached as an annex to the supply contract [Jerzy Kuzminski — fDBjJyTGWDQ @ 00:23:17]. Insurers joined before design and supplier choice to vet battery and transformer bankability [Lockton Europe — UI-9nmVEA9U @ 00:08:38]. Pushing harder wears the battery quicker.

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 5 is complete only when the power-versus-energy requirement is stated, the AC block and skid budget are broken down, the EMS is set to the real site, commissioning limits are locked, the parcel passes the grid-distance and upgrade-cost screen, and the warranty window and supplier bankability are documented.

worksheets.title: Data Center BESS Integration, Safety and Community Risk
worksheets.purpose: Prove the battery can hold an AI campus together at the point of interconnection and that the campus can survive the public hearing. This worksheet covers load swings, islanding, harmonics, fire listing, yard thermal design, incident response, community opposition, noise, water, land-deal signals and the decentralized alternative.
instructions: Describe the AI load in milliseconds and in percent of campus load, never in averages.
Collect validated models, EMT and harmonic studies and UL listing evidence before any purchase order is released.
Run airflow simulation at 30% and 60% design and test moderate wind rather than calm air before freezing the container layout.
Treat local opposition as an organized force; record polls, votes, moratoria and ballot measures with dates and sources.
Document every siting factor in writing, because documentation, not the score itself, is the legal shield.

fields.name: load_swing_profile
fields.prompt: Describe the AI training load behavior the battery must absorb, including step size as a share of campus load, the speed of the swing, and voltage-dip trip risk. State whether the solution is software smoothing, hardware, or both.
fields.example: Training load jumps 30-60% in milliseconds, so a grid-forming BESS is treated as the price of interconnection. Hardware chosen: Lyten's mobile system flattened up to 99.5% of load-step volatility in controlled tests and held voltage within +/-0.4% [Volta Foundation — 7h6DABJ_xgs @ 00:18:08]. Protection that makes sense inside the building can create risk outside it [Volta Foundation — 7h6DABJ_xgs @ 00:05:51].

fields.name: islanding_and_genset_strategy
fields.prompt: Record the BESS pickup time at full load, the upstream breaker opening time, and the total islanding target. State whether the battery supplements or replaces diesel gensets, the genset-delay duration sized, and how backup generators handle ride-through windows.
fields.example: BESS picks up full load in 20 ms with no bypass, so breaker opening sets the real limit and the system target is under 0.5 s [Digital Infrastructure Network — U2apRbTTZuE @ 00:08:45]. Battery supplements diesel and is sized at 1-2 h of genset delay. Gensets start but hold transfer until the ride-through window expires [Keentel Engineering — WN6PtJ3kQDQ @ 00:13:03].

fields.name: harmonics_and_model_validation
fields.prompt: List the validated vendor inverter models received, the EMT and harmonic studies completed, and the total demand distortion measured at the point of common coupling. Confirm every item was in hand before the purchase order was released.
fields.example: Validated inverter models obtained and EMT plus harmonic studies run, with compliance measured as TDD at the PCC, all before the purchase order, because a BESS is fundamentally a power electronic converter with a battery attached [Keentel Engineering — BTkszCEW7nY @ 00:00:17]. Some of these stability problems can only be solved at the grid interconnection [Volta Foundation — 7h6DABJ_xgs @ 00:21:07].

fields.name: fire_listing_and_testing
fields.prompt: Record the UL 9540 listing, the 9540A edition and installation-level fire test data, and whether the manufacturer allows the planned indoor or outdoor installation. Note the energy and spacing that trigger the large-scale fire test and the local fire official's stance.
fields.example: UL 9540 listing and full-scale fire test data confirmed, and the manufacturer permits outdoor installation [ALL4 Environmental Consultants — -B0ACVnCSu0 @ 00:18:02]. Units hold 100 kWh at 2 ft spacing, which triggers the NFPA 855 Chapter 9 test against a 50 kWh at 3 ft baseline [UL Solutions — TtbHyJ6xzNg @ 00:15:29]. Two weeks of preparation booked for about one day of testing.

fields.name: container_yard_thermal_layout
fields.prompt: Describe the container yard layout, spacing and airflow assumptions, including exhaust reingestion and intake temperature limits. Record the dates full-site airflow simulation ran at 30% and 60% design, the wind case tested, and drainage beneath high-voltage equipment.
fields.example: Airflow simulated at 30% and 60% design using worst-case moderate wind, not calm air [Rand Simulation — LBt7MoTnFFQ @ 00:14:15]. At 50% reingestion, 45C intake climbs to 50C and exhaust to 60C, nearing the 54C intake threshold [Rand Simulation — LBt7MoTnFFQ @ 00:21:35]. Grading keeps water from gathering beneath high-voltage equipment [Civil and Structural Engineer — 935Rt3dBZso @ 00:03:10].

fields.name: post_incident_and_scada_plan
fields.prompt: Name the cleanup lead and safety person in the post-incident plan, the handling method for cells holding stranded energy, and the SCADA data volume and retention specification. Note the event-transmission tests completed and whether switchgear supports remote monitoring and control.
fields.example: Post-incident plan written before energization, naming a cleanup lead and safety person and covering steel-drum handling of cells with stranded energy [ALL4 Environmental Consultants — -B0ACVnCSu0 @ 00:44:47]. SCADA specified for high data volume and retention, with DNP3 event transmission tested for buffer overflow [Australian Control Engineering | Smart Utilities — 8eadjA6Pqyo @ 00:00:20]. Digital switchgear supports remote control.

fields.name: community_opposition_scan
fields.prompt: Summarize local sentiment toward the campus, listing the top grievances raised, any moratoria or ballot measures nearby, and recent commission votes on comparable projects. Name the residents' groups active and the meetings where the project could surface.
fields.example: Polling shows 65% opposed, with electricity at 72%, water at 64% and noise at 41% as top grievances [PBS NewsHour — fkB8mt1DEVw @ 00:04:45]. Project Tango's expansion was denied 5-1 by the Palm Beach County Commission [WPLG Local 10 — iYCYPKhdqcY @ 00:05:09]. Of 41 Ohio county ballot initiatives, 40 ban sites above 25 MW [Latitude Media — D7D1CPOoub4 @ 00:50:40].

fields.name: noise_and_water_disclosure
fields.prompt: Record the fence-line noise readings in dBC or dBZ for continuous 24/7 operation, not dBA alone, and the cooling water answer. State whether any closed loop is filled once or draws water daily, and the indirect water from power generation.
fields.example: Fence-line noise reported in dBC and dBZ for 24/7 operation rather than dBA alone [Careers Over Beers Podcast — S_6FoEr75bs @ 00:11:30]. Closed loop confirmed as filled once rather than drawing water every day [PBS NewsHour — fkB8mt1DEVw @ 00:10:45]. Indirect water from power generation is estimated at two to three times direct use [Asianometry — tJYSzc7YkY0 @ 00:05:33].

fields.name: land_deal_and_permit_watch
fields.prompt: List any NDA or temporary lease offers tied to the parcel, the monthly check of diesel-generator air-permit filings, and the documentation kept for each siting factor. Note any solar pitch that could pivot to hyperscale after signature.
fields.example: A temporary solar lease offered under NDA is logged as the opening move of a data-center deal [Democracy Now! — Ac0-fBK0LVQ @ 00:03:27]. Diesel-generator air-permit filings are pulled once a month to catch backup generation before a hearing [Careers Over Beers Podcast — S_6FoEr75bs @ 01:16:47]. Every siting factor is documented, since documentation is the legal shield [Jeff Pierson — CmmE71lfGdw @ 00:06:08].

fields.name: decentralized_alternative
fields.prompt: Compare the hyperscale plan against a smaller distributed option on cost per megawatt, build time, site size and power-queue position. Note any district-heating pairing, the storage plan for spiky inference loads on distribution circuits, and the cooling approach proposed.
fields.example: Distributed node priced at a claimed $3M per MW and six months, against $15M per MW and 3-5 years for a 100 MW campus [Latitude Media — D7D1CPOoub4 @ 00:20:50]. A 20 MW build paired with district heating gets ahead in power allocation [Data Center Sales & Marketing Institute (DCSMI) — W92xU-lo1Gc @ 00:02:43]. Storage covers spiky inference loads.

worksheets.completion_gate: Worksheet 6 is complete only when the load-swing profile and islanding timeline are recorded, validated models and TDD at the PCC are in hand before the purchase order, UL 9540 listing and fire test data are confirmed, the yard layout passes airflow simulation, a post-incident plan is written, and community, noise, water and land-deal risks are documented.
